Pathway Description
G protein-coupled receptor (GPCR) signaling There are more than 800 GPR genes in the genome. These receptors activate adenylyl cyclase to produce cAMP from ATP, or in the phosphatidylinositol pathway, to produce a cell response, depending on the context. Sixteen of these receptors were deregulated in our tumor series (available upon request).
EGFR signaling This receptor was markedly upregulated. In addition, SC561 (present in cytosol) was upregulated in this pathway.
ErB2 signaling The ligand NR1C and its receptors ErnB2 and ErbB3 were upregulated. The ErpB4 interacting protein (ERBPBDP) was also upregulated. However, the ErB4 signaling pathway was not deregulated.
Integrin cell surface interactions Integrin dlb β3 signaling presented four upregulated elements. The αβ4 (A4) precursor protein-binding family B member Interacting protein (ABPPBIU) and downstream effector TAILN (TALN) were upregulated. This upregulation provided the activation of integrin subunit δβ3 and the subsequent activation of tyrosine-protein kinase SYK (SYK), which was also upregulated, by Src.
